name: IN-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans R+15 and incumbent Jim Baird is seeking re-election
Baird holds a roughly 20-to-1 fundraising edge over Drew Cox, plus about $537K in outside support
Polymarket prices Cox's win chance near 4%
$200K in outside spending opposing Baird is the only notable Democratic-side signal
model.rationale: An R+15 district, an incumbent running again, and a fundraising gap of roughly twenty to one leave Drew Cox without a visible path; betting markets price a Baird win around 94%, and no polling or expert ratings point to a competitive race.
model.watch: The $200,000 in outside spending against Baird is the only sign of Democratic investment; a late poll showing a much tighter race or a surge in Cox's fundraising would warrant a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 4th District is firmly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly fifteen points toward the GOP, and incumbent Jim Baird is seeking re-election. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on the district's lean, the money gap, and betting markets. Polymarket gives Democrat Drew Cox about a 4% chance of winning.

The financial mismatch is stark: Baird has raised about $358,000 and benefits from roughly $537,000 in outside support, while Cox has raised about $20,000 with minimal cash on hand. About $200,000 in outside spending is directed against Baird, the one signal of outside Democratic interest, but it is small against the district's lean. All available evidence points to a comfortable Republican hold.
